The new site lets the photos sell, shows the proof before the promise, and gives every visitor a short path to a quote request.

01 · The site today

What we found, point by point

Reviewed on 23 October on the live site, on desktop and mobile. Each number on the screenshot shows where the issue appears. Click a number to highlight it.

Current home page, full length, at desktop width.

Left: the home page on a phone. The first screen is only a photo. Right: the whole Bespoke Kitchens page, with a single image.

First impression the first five seconds

1The opening photo isn't your best workcritical

A light kitchen with blue LED ceiling lighting, which dates it. Your archive has much stronger work: the black marble kitchen, the green kitchen, the hotels. The menu has no "Our Work" link and no quote button.

2The headline says nothing: "Welcome to Hogan Bespoke Furniture"critical

It doesn't say what you make, who for, or why choose you. The headline is the first thing both Google and visitors read.

3A wall of thin, light grey textimportant

Four paragraphs and a list before any project photo. The light grey type is hard to read on a phone, especially outdoors.

Trust and proof why people should believe you

4An image that may be a stock rendercritical

The "Bespoke Kitchens" slider and the kitchens page use the same grey kitchen with a round pendant light. It looks like a stock 3D render. If it isn't one of your kitchens, it should go.

5The company story is hidden halfway down the pageimportant

How the business started sits in small print under "About Sean Hogan". On the new site it moves to the About page, told in the company's voice, with the work always up front.

6The copy names another company: "Fine Edge Furniture"critical

There are also typos ("crate" on Kitchens, "pretences" on Wardrobes). Careful readers notice, and they tend to be the clients with the bigger budgets.

7One testimonial, no Google reviewsimportant

Rory & Clara from Dunmore East, over a blurred photo. No Google reviews and no commercial work anywhere on the site.

Enquiries from interest to a quote request

8A generic form: name, email, phone, "additional information"critical

You can't tell if it's a kitchen or a single door, which county, when, or what budget. The same button has three different labels: "Schedule", "Book a consultation" and "Get in touch".

9Three different addressesimportant

The footer says Unit 8. The contact page says Unit 10 and Unit 8. The official address is Unit 7 & 8. The email on the site (@hoganbespokefurniture.com) also needs to match the one you use today. Inconsistent details hurt your Google ranking.

Technical and content invisible, but it matters

–No Google Analytics, Meta Pixel or meta descriptioncritical

There's no way to know where enquiries come from, and Google writes your search listing for you.

–The "Our Work" gallery exists but isn't in the menuimportant

hoganbespokefurniture.com/our-work/ has 14 photos, and almost nobody finds it. Each service page has one image.

–Elementor Pro is out of date (April 2023 version)important

A plugin with no updates for three years is a security risk. WordPress itself is up to date.

What already works and we'll keep

keepIt's fast

The home page opens in under a second on desktop.

keepAn established domain

hoganbespokefurniture.com has been on Google since 2022. The address stays the same.

keepYour brand

Black, graphite and oak, with the Alice serif. A good base that just needs room to breathe.

03 · Design principles

Five rules behind every screen

Photos sell

People buy bespoke with their eyes. Large photos with consistent colour and very little text over them. The story goes underneath the image, not on top of it.

Proof before promises

Real projects, commercial client names and Google reviews come before any line about "quality" or "excellence".

One path per visitor

Homes and commercial are separate from the menu down. Every page ends with a clear next step.

Easy to ask for a quote

One button, "Get a quote", always visible. A short step-by-step form that qualifies each enquiry for you.

Built for phones

Most visitors will come from Instagram, on a phone. Readable text, a fixed bar to call or get a quote, and light images.

10 · Behind the scenes

Tracking, Google and technology

Our agreement promises you'll know where every client comes from. This is what makes the monthly report possible.

Tracking

  • Google Analytics 4visits, most-viewed pages, where people come from
  • Meta Pixelsee who came from Instagram and, later, advertise to past visitors
  • Enquiry eventsquote sent, call tapped, email tapped
  • Tracked linksInstagram bio, LinkedIn, Google and brochures, each tagged
  • "How did you hear about us?"on the form, to capture referrals

Google (local SEO)

  • A title and description for each pagee.g. "Bespoke Kitchens in Ireland, handmade in Waterford"
  • Local business data (schema)name, address, phone and service area, matching your Google profile
  • A description on every photo"oak staircase, Co. Waterford" instead of "IMG_2041"
  • Search Consolesee which searches the site shows up for
  • Redirects from old pages/bespoke-kitchens/ goes to /kitchens/, so no ranking is lost

Technology

  • Same domain, accounts in your nameas set out in our agreement
  • WordPress, rebuilt from scratchadding the monthly case study is simple
  • Built on a test site firstthe current site stays live until you approve the new one
  • Optimised images and cachingtarget: under 2.5 seconds to open on a phone
  • Google reviews on the sitea widget linked to your Google Business profile
